To: chefmarket:review:KCK-4471
Replying to: [l01]
Cc: none
Subject: Refurbished Vantorre CX-10

We paid $14,800 including GST for this refurbished Vantorre CX-10, delivered and commissioned on 14 September with a six-month parts and labour warranty.

The listing said the steam generator had been descaled and pressure tested and the core probe calibrated. Within the first week we were getting E34, the steam generator low-water-level fault, with intermittent lockouts in steam and combi modes. The service report recorded nine E34 errors since delivery. On 22 September, Dion replaced the level sensor and tested three steam cycles successfully under warranty.

E34 returned four times the following week. We also checked the core probe twice against our Thermapen in a lamb shoulder: the oven read 63°C and the Thermapen 70°C both times. On 6 October, Dion found the steam generator heavily scaled, descaled and flushed it, and recalibrated the probe to within one degree.

Kelsall recommended a water softener, attributing the scale to our supply. We checked with the water company, which advised that Fitzroy’s average hardness is about 15 mg/L as CaCO3 and is soft. The oven had been on our water for only around three weeks when the heavy scale was found. That raises a reasonable question about its condition on delivery, particularly given the listing’s descaling claim.

On Saturday 24 October, E34 locked us out at 6.10 pm with 60 covers booked. We finished the lamb on the stove and in the deck oven, took pork belly off the menu and absorbed the cost. E34 was present again at the 27 October attendance, when further scale was found. Kelsall says this was a site water issue and has advised a $280 callout plus GST, or $308, despite the unit being about six weeks old and under warranty.

Dion has been helpful throughout, but the recurring fault, the scale finding and the proposed charge are concerns worth knowing about before spending this much on a refurbished unit.
